turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_max_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_max_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST yield strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training data show a clear dominance of heat_treatment=solution_aged combined with route=wrought for the highest 0.2 % proof stresses (multiple examples 650–713 MPa). Quench-and-temper + wrought reaches only ~580–611 MPa; solution-aged AM reaches ~620–637 MPa; annealed and most quenched conditions are substantially weaker. Within the solution-aged + wrought subset the highest values further cluster at C \(\approx\) 0.1–0.6 wt%, Fe \(\approx\) 63–78 wt%, aging temperatures 630–710 °C and aging times of a few tens of minutes (very short or very long times and aging temperatures \(\gtrsim\) 735 °C are associated with a modest drop, consistent with under-/over-aging).

Nine pool members satisfy solution-aged + wrought. Direct composition-plus-processing analogues to the strongest training points immediately rank them:

- c008 is nearly identical to a 649 MPa training alloy (and close to the 698 MPa alloy) and sits inside the 680–710 °C peak-aging window \(\to\) highest predicted strength.
- c053 matches the Cr–Ni–Fe balance of the 694 MPa alloy; the higher aging temperature is offset by a very short time, analogous to other 620–650 MPa examples \(\to\) second.
- c072 shares the low-Cr, high-Co/Mo/V signature of the 649 MPa alloy; its 750 °C age is slightly beyond the observed peak (cf. 628 MPa at 735 °C) \(\to\) third.
- c021 is compositionally close to the 668 MPa alloy (C near 0, moderate Cr/Ni/Mo) with a still-acceptable 592 °C age \(\to\) fourth.
- c038 reproduces the 613 MPa training point (high Fe, modest Cr/Ni, aging \(\approx\) 610 °C) \(\to\) fifth.

All remaining pool members (other heat-treatment/route combinations, extreme C, very low Fe, or aging temperatures well outside 600–720 °C) are predicted to lie below this group.

Final: c008, c053, c072, c021, c038
